edges.description: Slow washout favors local accumulation of thrombotic material.
Fragments of web-associated thrombus can be carried into downstream cerebral or retinal arteries.
Persistent downstream occlusion can cause cerebral infarction.
A persistent thrombogenic lesion can produce further ipsilateral embolic events.
intermediate_mechanisms: renewed local thrombus formation and embolization

nodes.description: Antiplatelet therapy is commonly used after symptomatic events, including alongside revascularization. Anticoagulation has also been used in selected patients or for other indications. The optimal agent, combination and duration for the web itself are not established; recurrence can occur on therapy.
nodes.id: Antithrombotic medical therapy after symptomatic ischemia

evidence.reference_title: Carotid Web: An Update Focusing on Its Relationship With Fibromuscular Dysplasia and Therapeutic Strategy.
evidence.snippet: Treatment options in symptomatic cases include medical therapy (single or dual antiplatelets) or interventional approach (surgery or stenting), but there are no randomized controlled trials about therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Stroke Recurrence in First-Ever Symptomatic Carotid Web: A Cohort Study.
evidence.snippet: All patients treated with carotid surgery or stenting received long-term antithrombotic therapy with aspirin (n=21) or vitamin K antagonist (n=2) that was ongoing at the end of follow-up.

evidence.reference_title: In-hospital recurrent stroke in ipsilateral carotid web patients undergoing thrombectomy.
evidence.snippet: the benefit of immediate dual antiplatelet or anticoagulation therapy remains unclear, particularly in medium to large strokes where there is an elevated risk of hemorrhage

nodes.description: Language dysfunction can be part of the presenting ischemic event.

evidence.reference_title: Outcomes after carotid revascularization for symptomatic carotid artery web: A multi-institutional cohort study.
evidence.snippet: The most common presenting symptoms were hemibody numbness/weakness, aphasia, and gaze deviation.

nodes.description: Detachment and transport of web-associated thrombus can occlude downstream vessels. Ischemic manifestations depend on the affected vascular territory and whether perfusion is restored before infarction.

evidence.reference_title: Stroke Recurrence in First-Ever Symptomatic Carotid Web: A Cohort Study.
evidence.snippet: The widely accepted mechanism of cerebral ischemic events (CIE) is an artery-to-artery embolism through blood stasis rostral to CaW, thrombus formation and clot fragmentation scattered by the blood flow

nodes.description: Stenting across the web is used to exclude the thrombogenic pouch in selected symptomatic patients. The 71-person multicenter series included 48 stenting and 23 endarterectomy procedures, with one perioperative stroke overall and one recurrent stroke in the stenting group. Procedure selection was not randomized and there was no medical-only control.

evidence.reference_title: Outcomes after carotid revascularization for symptomatic carotid artery web: A multi-institutional cohort study.
evidence.snippet: CAS was undertaken in 48 patients (67.6%) and CEA in 23 (32.4%). One patient (1.41%) experienced a perioperative stroke, and none experienced a perioperative MI

evidence.reference_title: Outcomes after carotid revascularization for symptomatic carotid artery web: A multi-institutional cohort study.
evidence.snippet: no recurrent strokes were observed in patients undergoing CEA, and one recurrent symptomatic stroke occurred in the CAS cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Carotid Revascularization Versus Medical Management for Ischemic Stroke with Ipsilateral Carotid Web: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: given the small, heterogeneous cohorts and the uncertain natural history of carotid artery web under medical management, these findings should be interpreted with caution until prospective, controlled comparative effectiveness studies are performed.

nodes.description: Selected symptomatic patients undergo surgical excision of the web, removing a local embolic source and permitting histological examination. Retrospective series report low recurrence but have no randomized medical control; cranial-nerve injury is a procedural risk.

evidence.reference_title: Pathologically Confirmed Symptomatic Carotid Webs: Histopathological Features and Long-Term Surgical Outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Among 39 patients with symptomatic carotid web, 34 underwent CEA with histopathological confirmation of the diagnosis, characterized by focal eccentric intimal fibromyxoid tissue, fibromuscular dysplasia, hyperplasia, or thickening.

evidence.reference_title: Pathologically Confirmed Symptomatic Carotid Webs: Histopathological Features and Long-Term Surgical Outcomes.
evidence.snippet: At a median follow-up of 29 months, no patients experienced recurrent stroke (95% CI: 0%-10%), and the median modified Rankin Scale score was 1 (0-1).

evidence.reference_title: Pathologically Confirmed Symptomatic Carotid Webs: Histopathological Features and Long-Term Surgical Outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Two patients experienced transient, minor cranial nerves injuries (hypoglossal nerve and marginal mandibular branch) after CEA.

evidence.reference_title: Carotid Revascularization Versus Medical Management for Ischemic Stroke with Ipsilateral Carotid Web: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.snippet: given the small, heterogeneous cohorts and the uncertain natural history of carotid artery web under medical management, these findings should be interpreted with caution until prospective, controlled comparative effectiveness studies are performed.

nodes.description: Retinal arterial infarction is an uncommon reported ischemic presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Stroke Recurrence in First-Ever Symptomatic Carotid Web: A Cohort Study.
evidence.snippet: At inclusion, 13 patients experienced a TIA as first-ever CIE and two patients suffered from a central retina artery infarction without any recent lesion on admission MRI.

nodes.description: The web geometry produces local flow separation, recirculation, low velocity and prolonged residence time. These abnormalities can occur with modest luminal narrowing.

evidence.reference_title: Subjects with carotid webs demonstrate pro-thrombotic hemodynamics compared to subjects with carotid atherosclerosis
evidence.snippet: Patients with CaW had significantly larger regions containing low shear rate, high OSI, low velocity, and flow stasis in comparison to subjects with mild atherosclerosis or normal bifurcations.

nodes.description: Ipsilateral ischemic stroke, often including large-vessel occlusion, is a major symptomatic presentation. The lesion may also be incidental, so stroke is not required to diagnose a web.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical, imaging, and management features of symptomatic carotid web: Insight from CAROWEB registry.
evidence.snippet: Between June 2019 and December 2021, 244 cases were submitted by 14 centers, 42 rejected, and 202 included (IS, 91.6%; TIA, 7.9%; retinal infarction, 0.5%; mean age, 50.8 ± 12.2 years; female, 62.9%; Caucasian, 47.5%; Afro-Caribbean, 20.3%).

nodes.description: Unilateral weakness may accompany carotid-web-associated cerebral ischemia; the distribution depends on the affected brain territory.

nodes.description: Eccentric fibrous and myxoid intimal tissue forms a shelf projecting into the arterial lumen. Smooth-muscle-like spindle cells are embedded in extracellular matrix; the lesion differs from a lipid-rich atheroma.
nodes.id: Intimal shelf lesion of the carotid bulb

evidence.reference_title: Histopathologic evidence of intimal hyperplasia in carotid artery webs associated with stroke.
evidence.snippet: Histopathologic analysis consistently demonstrated fibrovascular tissue with intimal fibroid hyperplasia and myxoid degeneration, without lipid-rich plaques or inflammatory infiltrates.

evidence.reference_title: Carotid Web: An Update Focusing on Its Relationship With Fibromuscular Dysplasia and Therapeutic Strategy.
evidence.snippet: The common histological feature of the carotid web is eccentric intimal hyperplasia, characterized by spindle cells (consistent with migrated vascular smooth muscle cells) intermingled within an abundant loose extracellular matrix.

nodes.description: Intravenous thrombolysis is another acute reperfusion treatment used in eligible web-associated strokes. It addresses the acute thrombotic occlusion and does not remove the intimal shelf.
nodes.id: Intravenous thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke

evidence.reference_title: Carotid revascularization is associated with reduced recurrence in symptomatic carotid web.
evidence.snippet: Fifteen (75%) underwent mechanical thrombectomy and 8 (40%) received IV thrombolysis.

nodes.description: Endovascular thrombectomy treats an eligible acute intracranial occlusion associated with a carotid web. It restores downstream patency but leaves the carotid lesion in place, so it does not establish a secondary-prevention strategy.

nodes.description: Further ipsilateral ischemic events can occur during the initial hospitalization or over subsequent years. Recurrence estimates vary with case selection, antithrombotic treatment and endpoint definition.

evidence.reference_title: In-hospital recurrent stroke in ipsilateral carotid web patients undergoing thrombectomy.
evidence.snippet: 11% (3/27) of patients with ipsilateral carotid artery webs experienced recurrent ischemic stroke and LVO.

nodes.description: TCAR is a stent-based approach reported for selected symptomatic webs. A 2026 series of 20 revascularized patients used TCAR in 65%, with no ipsilateral recurrent ischemic strokes during a median nine-month follow-up across all approaches. This small uncontrolled series does not establish superiority or long-term safety.

evidence.reference_title: Carotid revascularization is associated with reduced recurrence in symptomatic carotid web.
evidence.snippet: TCAR was the most common approach (65%), followed by CAS (20%) and CEA (15%).

evidence.reference_title: Carotid revascularization is associated with reduced recurrence in symptomatic carotid web.
evidence.snippet: Over a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR: 6-21), no patients experienced recurrent ischemic stroke in the treated vascular territory, suggesting potential effectiveness of revascularization in preventing recurrence in selected patients with carotid webs.
